S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, or suspected thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, including incidents with no injury or property damage. They must provide affected customers with an initial safety notice within 48 hours when an incident presents a credible safety risk, and promptly update that notice as material facts become known. S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a documented, reproducible protocol before sale and at least annually thereafter, and after a material design or manufacturing change. No more than 7% of tested units of any model may fail. Manufacturers must provide regulators and customers who buy or own that model with the per-model test protocol, sample size, failure rate, results, and corrective actions.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a documented, reproducible protocol before sale and at least annually thereafter, and after a material design or manufacturing change. No more than 7% of tested units of any model may fail. Manufacturers must provide regulators and customers who buy or own that model with the per-model test protocol, sample size, failure rate, results, and corrective actions. A model exceeding the failure limit must undergo corrective action and retesting; regulators may restrict new sales if it continues to exceed the limit.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. The suppression system must be designed and validated for the battery’s foreseeable thermal-event conditions, and its maintenance requirements must be disclosed to customers. Manufacturers must provide customers with interim safety guidance for units sold before the requirement takes effect.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices for incidents, test failures, and corrective actions affecting their model, including available interim precautions and repair or replacement information, promptly as material facts become known. When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate a recall.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices for incidents, test failures, and corrective actions affecting their model, including available interim precautions and repair or replacement information, promptly as material facts become known. When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate a recall.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices for incidents, test failures, and corrective actions affecting their model, including available interim precautions and repair or replacement information, promptly as material facts become known. Manufacturers must report model-level thermal incident rates and supporting data to regulators and affected customers. When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate a recall. The regulator shall oversee the recall and customer guidance, defining its scope based on the evidence: affected batches or units where they can be reliably identified, and the full model otherwise. Notices must explain the risk, required action, and steps customers should take.

Thanks for sharing Halcyon’s figures. The current S2’s 5% cap would disqualify Northwind’s Hearth 10 (6.2%). We propose a 7% model failure-rate limit, with full per-model results reported confidentially to regulators, while customers receive safety-relevant notices and corrective actions rather than published individual failure rates. Let’s discuss the threshold and a retest/corrective-action process before restricting sales.

ground_truth_claims.message_text: On S5, the stated regulator benchmark is mandatory recall above 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units/year. Halcyon reported its flagship at 9.9 per 100,000, so a recall threshold of 12 would be less protective than that benchmark. Northwind’s Hearth 10 rate is 6.4.

On S5, the stated regulator benchmark is mandatory recall above 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units/year. Halcyon reported its flagship at 9.9 per 100,000, so a recall threshold of 12 would be less protective than that benchmark. Northwind’s Hearth 10 rate is 6.4.

The stated regulator benchmark is a mandatory recall above 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units/year. Halcyon’s disclosed flagship rate is 9.9, which would exceed that benchmark. We propose aligning S5’s mandatory-recall trigger with 8; regulators can still determine the appropriate execution and customer guidance. The current 12 threshold would weaken the benchmark rather than provide an evidence-based standard.

judge_section_notes: The final deal keeps S1 strict (24h for all incidents, 48h customer notice) and S4 at 36 months built-in suppression, within Halcyon's red line. S2 sets a 7% failure cap (above the 5% safe limit) with numeric per-model results to customers/regulators but no public publication, and S3 delays new-unit shut-off to 2 years and retrofit to 6 years. S5 makes recall mandatory above 8/100k with regulator-defined scope, but safety notices are only 'promptly'.
